text:
emma: FYI customer acme-inc opened a support ticket — EU users seeing p99 jump from ~800ms to 3s+ starting ~06:30 UTC. Some requests show 504s. Ticket C-7891. Raising SRE for triage :rotating_light:

devon: seeing the alert on dashboards. p95 also up but p99 much worse. Affected path seems EU1 -> US core. No deployment at 06:30 in prod according to deploy-bot. Any infra change?

opsbot: alert: p99_latency.api-host (eu1) crossed 2.8s threshold at 1968799800, approx 06:32 UTC. Autocreated alert incident.inc/4642.

sam: I ran quick synthetic checks from eu1-pop and eu2-pop. Raw curl timings:
```
# from eu1-pop
$ curl -sS -w '%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer} %{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.example/health
0.150 0.450 3.12
# from eu2-pop
0.140 0.430 0.95
```
So eu2 looks fine, eu1 showing 3s. Traceroute/mtr indicates a big jump hitting hop 7 which crosses into a US transit.

sam: mtr snippet (condensed):
```
1  10.0.1.1       0.4% 20  0.6  0.7  0.4  1.2
2  isp-pe-01      0.0% 20  1.8  2.1  1.6  3.9
3  isp-core-03    0.0% 20 12.4 13.0 11.9 15.6
4  be-5-2.edge.isp.net 0.0% 20 150.2 152.3 149.8 160.9
5  ge-2.core.us-west.net 0.0% 20 900.4 912.0 899.1 950.1
```
That ~900ms hop is suspicious (path inflation crossing to US).

emma: customer says it started during a morning traffic spike. Could be routing flap / upstream peering. Any BGP churn on our side?

devon: control-plane BGP checks show no config changes, but I see transient BGP flaps from isp-edge between 06:28–06:35. RIB shows AS path temporarily prepended which may have pushed traffic over longer transit. Putting logs here: `grep 'bgp.*flap' /var/log/bgp-collector/06-15.log` shows multiple updates.

alex: on quick mitigation: we can force smart-routing policy for acme-inc to prefer eu-only backbone (we have a route preference override). Proposal: apply customer route override to pin to eu-pop and serve from nearest regional cache for 30m while we monitor. That would reduce p99 for them. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

sam: +1 from infra. To be safe also bump KV cache TTL for their session tokens to reduce cross-region calls.

devon: I'm going to test `--resolve` curl to force EU edge and compare:
```
# force eu-pop IP
curl -sS --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.12.5.7 https://api.redwood.example/health -w '%{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null
# result: 0.38
```
If forcing eu-pop gives sub-second response, then routing is root cause.

oncall-bot: automation: created temporary routing override policy ro-774 for customer acme-inc, expires in 30m. Change authored by alex.

emma: Alex, please apply and notify support so they can confirm with customer. Also add a note in ticket with repro commands (sam's curl).

alex: applied ro-774 and increased session token TTL from 60s -> 300s for acme-inc on eu-pop caches. Patching now. Rolling checks.

sam: after override, synthetic from eu1-pop -> 0.36s, p99 back under 900ms overall and acme-specific traces show sub-700ms. Still monitoring.

emma: customer reports improvement for a subset of users, still seeing some hits but much better. I'll keep them updated.

devon: follow-ups: need to open a ticket with ISP partner for AS-path prepends and ask for stable peering. Also add permanent route preference for enterprise-tier customers as an ops playbook item.

oncall-bot: incident classified P2, creating short postmortem stub: incidents/1968800000-eu-us-path-inflation. Assigned to devon/sam/alex.

emma: thanks team. After we stabilize, let's capture the exact BGP updates and confirm whether it was upstream prepending vs internal export issue. Also verify no config rollouts accidentally triggered the ISP to prefer a different transit.

devon: noted. I'll collect bgp collector dump and export to the incident. If anyone has packet captures from ~06:30 from eu1 egress, drop to the incident.

alex: adding runbook item: quick check list for cross-region latency spikes — curl resolve, mtr, check BGP flaps, temporary route override, bump TTLs, notify partner. Will PR to ops-runbooks after this is closed. :thumbsup:

emma: closing the thread here — monitoring for next 30m. If we see reoccurrence we'll escalate to P1. Thanks all.
